text:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT P1 — high memory growth on kv-cache workers in prod-rt-1. Observed steady allocation + fragmentation since 09:12 UTC. Auto-escalating to oncall. PAGER: @maya (oncall) :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing increased OOMs and long tail latencies on /generate routes. customer-ops flagged timeouts from 3 customers (SLA risk).

sam: logs show repeated cuda malloc failures then arena resizes. snippet of worker logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z worker-42 ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z kv-cache INFO slab_alloc(size=8192) -> arena 3 used 98%\n2026-03-15T09:12:05Z batch-engine WARN batch_size exceeded, fallback to single
```

zane: @maya can you confirm it's the continuous-batching path? we had a recent tweak to batch_threshold=0.45 in canary.

maya (oncall): yes, production config shows batch_threshold=0.45 across the pool. reducing now to 0.25 as emergency mitigation.

kai: also seeing high fragmentation counters from the allocator exporter: 
```
kv_allocator.frag_ratio 0.67
kv_allocator.free_slab_count 12
kv_allocator.largest_free 4MB
```

maya (oncall): running hotfix:
```
# set emergency feature flag to reduce continuous batching
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://config.internal/redwood/featureflags \
  -d '{"continuous_batch_threshold":0.25, "reason":"kv-frag emergency"}'
```

sam: starting staggered restart of batch workers in prod-rt-1 (10% per minute) to pick up change. kubectl rollout in progress.

incidents-bot: PAGERDUTY: Incident triggered on service=kv-cache, severity=page, escalation_policy=oncall-sre.

pagerduty-bot: Paging maya (oncall) and escalated to sre-lead if not acked in 5m.

maya (oncall): acked. monitoring memory RSS on the restarted pods. so far one pod restarted and memory dropped from 78GB -> 22GB after restart and compaction triggered.

zane: curious: are we hitting a PyTorch allocator regression? I see patterns like arena grow + not releasing to CUDA. stack traces show calls into at::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator.

sam: I pulled a coredump from worker-42. grep of stack traces:
```
# backtrace
0 at::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator::raw_alloc()
1 kv::allocator::arena::allocate_block()
2 kv::cache::insert_with_batching()
```

maya (oncall): temporary mitigation plan: 1) reduce batching aggressiveness (done), 2) nudge allocator to release unused arenas by toggling arena_release_hint, 3) enable KV compaction job on the pool, 4) schedule controlled canary of tuned pytorch build.

kai: commands to nudge allocator:
```
# toggle allocator tunable via admin endpoint
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/allocator/tunables -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"arena_release_delay_ms":1000, "max_arena_size_mb":256}'
```

sam: kicked the compaction job for prod-rt-1: compaction run id=202603150912-1. watching evictions.

maya (oncall): customer-ops: notified two customers about degraded performance and mitigation steps. severity: elevated. awaiting further impact reports.

zane: telemetry shows a drop in fragment_ratio from 0.67 -> 0.42 after two restarts and compaction starting. GPU mem pressure still spikes intermittently.

sre-lead: what's the rollback plan if compaction exacerbates latency?

maya (oncall): rollback: revert continuous_batch_threshold to previous value and cancel compaction job. we've got staging verified rollback playbook.

incidents-bot: NOTE: automated rollback guard - if 95th latency on /generate > 1.5x baseline for 2m, abort compaction.

sam: telemetry note: we saw one worker hit cuda OOM at 09:26 while compaction was in progress. we marked that pod as unhealthy and removed from rotation.

maya (oncall): can we apply a patch to batch-engine that short-circuits batch growth when allocator frag exceeds threshold? would require quick binary change.

zane: quick patch idea: if allocator_frag_ratio > 0.6 then force max_batch_tokens=128. I can build a canary.

maya (oncall): prioritize compaction + tunable flips for now. canary patch if fragmentation re-spikes.

kai: running lightweight probe to confirm whether PyTorch version X.Y.Z bump is correlated: comparing nvprof traces between  X.Y.Z and X.Y.(Z-1). early sign: newer release introduced different caching behavior.

pagerduty-bot: reminder: if incident continues > 2h, escalate to SEV board.

maya (oncall): current status at 09:38 UTC: continuous batching reduced, compaction job running, two pods drained/restarted. observed client error rate down from 2.8% -> 0.6%. keeping page open for observation.

sam: adding runbook note: 'emergency: reduce continuous_batch_threshold, trigger arena compaction, stagger restart, toggle arena_release_delay' — will capture exact commands in postmortem.

zane: I'll start building the patched batch-engine with guardrails. will canary in one AZ.

maya (oncall): customer-ops confirmed one customer saw partial request loss during the spike; we offered credits and will follow up with root cause once postmortem ready.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: reduced scope to prod-rt-1 cluster only. not global. severity: P1 -> P2 candidate pending stability for 30m.

maya (oncall): leaving a short checklist for follow-up ops: [compaction logs, core dump analysis, pytorch version diff, batch-engine patch test, customer impact timeline]. assigning owners: sam=compaction & restarts, zane=allocator root cause, kai=pytorch traces, maya=postmortem draft & comms.

sre-lead: thanks team. if metrics stay stable for 45m we can declare mitigated and begin post-incident review.

maya (oncall): leaving the channel but will be reachable. tagging handoff to zane for night watch. :white_check_mark:

zane: taking watch. will update at 10:20 UTC or earlier if things change.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVE SCHEDULED: please close thread after postmortem created.
